real.Milestone: M3.1, no symbols. With the oracle's own 18 symbols supplied it is 0.9970/0.8579; ./build.sh Fidelity reports both. The ratchet is the without-symbols number because that is what `skala format` does with no project.

constructs.Milestone: M10, formatter tags: constructs/arrangement/formatter-tags/ adds three files to the set, taking it from 324 to 327. All three are byte-identical to CSReformatCode's answer, so the number rises rather than falls — which is the point of committing them: the oracle honours the tags under the format-only profile and ignores them under the cleanup profile (SK-DIV-0016), and the .arranged.expected.cs beside each of these is where that is pinned. M9 was 324 files at 0.9745/0.9228.

pathological.Milestone: ⚠ The one baseline in this file that has been LOWERED, and the argument is SK-DIV-0018. Four more fuzz reproductions were retired into the set (54 to 59): SK-FUZZ-0002's, -0003's, -0004's, and SK-FUZZ-0007's pair. Five of the six match the oracle byte for byte and raised the number to 0.9649/0.8966; mixed-line-endings-after-a-trailing-comment.cs then took it to 0.9589/0.8814 on its own. That file's three lines are SK-DIV-0018 entire — on a file whose endings are ALREADY mixed the oracle normalises the whole file to one ending and Skala keeps each gap's own, which is what `enforce_line_ending_style = false` says. It is not reachable on any internally consistent file, and crlf-throughout.cs and mixed-crlf-and-lf.cs are both still exact. ⚠ The alternative was to leave the reproduction out of the corpus, and that is the wrong instinct: docs/plan/12 says the corpus only grows, the pathological set exists to hold the files that are hard, and a minimised reproduction dropped because it embarrasses a number is a measurement managing its own result. M10 was 54 files at 0.9636/0.8889.
